clue.text: Lead astray a group of apprentices

indicators.note: a group of letters is picked out of the following word, so the answer sits inside it

blocks.note: the run of letters after the opening APPR

explanation.surface: A gang of trainees is led into mischief by someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice someone is to tempt or lure them, which is leading them astray.

clue.text: One taking flight may have one, though one taking flight may not?

definitions.text: One taking flight may have one, though one taking flight may not?

blocks.clueFragment: One taking flight may have one
blocks.note: surface reading: an air passenger flying abroad may carry a certain travel document

blocks.clueFragment: though one taking flight may not
blocks.note: setter's reading: someone fleeing the country secretly, taking flight in the other sense, would not have official permission to leave

explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking flight' is used twice: first as boarding a plane, then as running away. Some states require a document before a citizen may leave.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the official permit some countries demand before a person is allowed to depart, which an escapee would lack.

clue.text: Better spinner

blocks.note: first meaning: as a verb, to outdo or surpass
second meaning: a toy that spins on its point

explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' reads as an adjective, but it is the verb meaning to improve on.
explanation.definitionFit: To top a score is to beat it, and a top is the classic spinning toy.

clue.text: French painter capturing extremely nice circlet

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two end letters only
to capture is to hold something inside, so one piece is held within another

blocks.note: first and last letters of nice

explanation.surface: A French artist pockets a lovely little band of jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: NE goes in just before Corot's final T.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronet is a small crown, a decorative circlet worn on the head.

clue.text: Well-defined remedy

blocks.note: second meaning: a medicine aimed at one particular disease

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means exact, and as a noun it names a drug targeted at one condition.

clue.text: A type of French dressing?

blocks.note: surface reading: a vinaigrette for salad
setter's reading: a dressing for broken limbs named after a French city

explanation.walkthrough: French dressing is a salad sauce; here the dressing is a medical one, and its name includes the French capital.
explanation.definitionFit: This gypsum material is used to set casts on fractures, a surgical dressing named after the city where it was mined.

clue.text: Examine almost all of hotel register

indicators.note: almost all means the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: an inn is a small hotel

explanation.surface: An inspector looks over most of a hotel's guest book.
explanation.definitionFit: To check in is to register on arrival at a hotel or airport, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Struggling with fish in middle of Niger

indicators.note: the middle of a five-letter word is its third letter alone

explanation.surface: Someone has trouble with a fish caught in the middle of the African river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a placement instruction, but it is simply two letters of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Floundering means thrashing about helplessly, so it is a synonym for struggling.

clue.text: Tenor to sing mostly round America

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word, so its last letter goes
going round something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: to carol is to sing joyfully

explanation.surface: A tenor sings most of the time while touring America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' sits after 'mostly', so the shortening happens before the wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Enrico Caruso was the celebrated Italian operatic tenor, an example of the category.

clue.text: Unexceptional order — gammon about to be eaten by inmate

indicators.note: about here means turned about, so the letters before it are rearranged
what is eaten goes inside the eater, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: a con is a convict, a prison inmate

explanation.surface: A prisoner's ordinary meal: gammon ordered up and eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled letters go between the O and N of CON.
explanation.definitionFit: Common or garden is an idiom for ordinary, nothing out of the usual.

clue.text: Copy some painter, uncannily

indicators.note: uncannily suggests something weirdly altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist's work is imitated with eerie accuracy.
explanation.definitionFit: To impersonate someone is to mimic them, a verb synonym for copy.

clue.text: Blade in centre of boat on river

indicators.note: the centre of a four-letter word is its two inner letters

blocks.note: the two middle letters of boat
R is the standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A sharp blade lies in the middle of a boat out on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blade' is a rower's word for this, the flat part or the whole implement.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing oar is often called a blade, especially in racing, a sporting synonym.

clue.text: One carried by experienced soldier, soldier returning from Asian country

indicators.note: something carried is held within its carrier, so one piece goes inside another
returning means coming back the way it went, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a man is a private soldier

explanation.surface: A veteran carries a comrade home from service in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: The single letter goes just after the first letter of the veteran; 'Nam is also American veterans' slang for this country.
explanation.definitionFit: Vietnam is a nation in South-East Asia, an example of the category.

clue.text: Cairo rowers worried environmental activists

indicators.note: something worried is shaken about, as a dog worries a bone, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Egyptian oarsmen are bothered by green campaigners.
explanation.definitionFit: Eco-warriors is a name for militant campaigners for the natural world, a synonym.

clue.text: Receipts given out by volunteers at Cambridge college

blocks.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Volunteers at a Cambridge college hand out receipts.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's part-time volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Takings are the money a business receives, a plural-noun synonym for receipts.

clue.text: Filming mountain chain where guns may be fired

blocks.note: to shoot a film is to film it
a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: A film crew on location in the mountains, near where guns go off.
explanation.walkthrough: Shooting first reads as filmmaking, then the definition reclaims it for firearms.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting range is a facility set aside for target practice with firearms.

clue.text: Song about a leader in army, detested person

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round a single letter
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A song about an army commander who is widely loathed.
explanation.walkthrough: ANTHEM wraps the A after its first two letters, then the army's first letter follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Anathema means something or someone intensely loathed, from a word for a cursed thing.

clue.text: Following a trend? Not completely

blocks.note: first meaning: read literally, coming after a vogue
second meaning: the idiom for in a rough or partial way

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the first definition takes the phrase word by word: after means following and a fashion a trend.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to some extent but not very well, so it says something is done only partially.

clue.text: Loud cry coming from Tarzan's mouth, and strange tamed animal

indicators.note: a word's mouth is its opening, so only its first letter is kept

blocks.note: rum is British slang for odd
a pet is a domesticated animal

explanation.surface: Tarzan's famous jungle yell summons an odd tame creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' looks like an anagram signal, but it is RUM, old-fashioned British slang for peculiar.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumpet is the loud call of an elephant, so the word names a bellowing noise.

clue.text: Military governor holding butt of latest weapon

indicators.note: the butt of something is its end, so only the last letter counts
holding something means having it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a shogun was a Japanese military ruler

explanation.surface: A general grips the stock of the newest firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butt' teasingly suggests a gun's stock, but it means the tail end of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A shotgun is a smooth-bore firearm, an example of a weapon.

clue.text: Far out, she exploded again

indicators.note: out suggests disordered or put wrong, so the word before it is rearranged
something exploded is blown apart, so the word before it is jumbled

blocks.note: the first set of letters to be rearranged
the second set of letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Far out, she lost her temper once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Afresh is an adverb meaning anew, a synonym for again.

clue.text: Very unpleasant about jolly adult providing powdered milk for babies

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round another

blocks.note: a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A grumpy grown-up made the baby's bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' looks like an adjective, but a jolly is a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM.
explanation.definitionFit: Formula is the manufactured milk substitute for feeding infants, a specific sense of the word.

clue.text: With a feeling of apprehension, ringing doctor

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so one word goes round another

explanation.surface: Someone nervously phones a physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' looks like a link to the rest of the clue, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Amongst means in the company of, as with in 'living with wolves', a preposition synonym.

clue.text: Personal pride, for example, shown by first of opponents

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of the word is kept

explanation.surface: A competitor shows self-regard against rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: Ego is a sense of self-importance or self-esteem, a synonym for personal pride.

clue.text: Lad ending up lost, not far from London Bridge

indicators.note: something lost has wandered astray, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A boy has got himself lost near a London landmark.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes a place: this City of London street, where the Great Fire of 1666 began, runs near London Bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The street lies a short walk from the bridge, so a location description serves as its definition.

clue.text: A party in trouble

explanation.surface: A celebration goes badly wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado means fuss or bother, so it serves as a noun synonym for trouble.

clue.text: Male worker, about model, is uncertain

indicators.note: about means around, so two words go round another

blocks.note: to sit for an artist is to model

explanation.surface: A man employed as an artist's model can't make up his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: HE and ANT together wrap SIT; the worker is the insect, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitant describes someone wavering or unsure, so it is an adjective synonym for uncertain.

clue.text: Mohair — an artist going round to buy it?

blocks.note: a go is a round or turn in a game

explanation.surface: An artist travels round to purchase some woolly fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: The artist goes after the round. The question mark nods to Angora, the old name for Ankara, the Turkish city that gave the goat its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Mohair is cloth from the Angora goat, so the breed's name serves for the fabric.
